fixtures.city_amends_note: No city change to the toilet counts was found. Little Rock enforces the 2018 Arkansas Plumbing Code, and the city's commercial handout sends the count to the state: an applicant submits a certificate or letter of approval from the Arkansas Department of Health for work involving plumbing facilities, and the Health Department's review covers the 'Statement of occupant load for determining minimum number of bathroom facilities' and 'Approval for the use of unisex bathrooms'. City Code Chapter 8 (plumbing article) could not be read on Municode, so this is medium confidence. The city's Tenant Space Checklist (September 2018, written for the older code) says a unisex restroom is allowed under 16 occupants; the 2018 Arkansas Plumbing Code read in the state pack says 25 or fewer, so the page keeps the state pack's 25.

The city's fee ordinance requires a permit for work over $5,000 (material and labor) or work that requires an inspection, and excludes painting, floor coverings and 'cosmetic changes'. page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Little Rock job sites. Price your restroom, pick a material and see the Little Rock rules that apply.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Little Rock state offices, hospitals, schools and warehouses, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Little Rock enforces Arkansas's plumbing rules, which set the number of toilets by how many people use the building. The table below shows what that means. On commercial plumbing work the city asks for an approval letter from the Arkansas Department of Health, which checks the count.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Little Rock requires a permit for any work that costs more than $5,000, material and labor together, or that needs an inspection. Painting, floor coverings and cosmetic changes are excluded. The state building rules the city enforces also exempt finish work such as painting, tiling and cabinets, and movable partitions no taller than 5 feet 9 inches. Neither list names toilet partitions, so ask the Building Codes Division permit desk (501-371-4832) whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.confirm_office: the Little Rock Building Codes Division
page.install_rule: Contractors pulling permits in Little Rock pay a city business license fee and get a contractor card for each type of work. The city's permit desk also asks for a $10,000 surety bond made out to the City. Arkansas requires a license from the Arkansas Contractors Licensing Board for commercial jobs of $50,000 or more, labor and materials together. Confirm what your project needs with the Little Rock Building Codes Division. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: A contractor who takes out a permit in Little Rock needs a city business license.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** Arkansas repealed its wage law for public jobs in 2017, so a set wage applies only on federally funded work. The federal rate for a carpenter on building work in Pulaski County is $17.51 an hour plus $2.26 in benefits.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 8.625% in Little Rock: 6.5% state, 1% Pulaski County and 1.125% city.
page.buyers_extra: - **State offices and hospitals:** phenolic or stainless steel for restrooms that are busy and cleaned often.
